subject: [Recap] Acme renewal & expansion call — usage, new workloads, next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Patel <sana.patel@acmecorp.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmecorp.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Renewal & expansion call (today) — usage, pain points, next steps

Hi Sana / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and next steps so we all have a shared view. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of what we covered:
- Current footprint: ~120M tokens/month across prod and staging, primarily text-generation for customer support workflows.
- Pain points: rising per-token cost during peak, latency spikes on long-context prompts (~2.5–3s p95), and cold-start time for nightly batch jobs.
- New workloads: planning to add an internal summarization pipeline for agent transcripts and a re-ranking step for search re-ranking (Q3).
- Goals for renewal: renew current committed capacity, add reserved Dedicated pool for the summarization workload, and pilot embeddings-based rerank.

Proposed upsell path (from call):
1) Q3 pilot: Dedicated pool (2x A10 GPUs equivalent) for summarization (1–2 month pilot)
2) If pilot meets latency/cost targets, convert to reserved capacity starting Oct 1
3) Add embeddings units for rerank as a separate line item (estimate below)

Action items & owners:
- Redwood (Marissa): send updated quote + SOW with pilot details and timeline (attached). Target: by Thu 6/30.
- Redwood (Vivek): confirm expected p95 latency and batching settings for summarization workload; share KB on batching/quant profiles. Target: Tue 7/6.
- Acme (Sana): share a short sample of the transcript data format and expected daily volume for summarization. Target: Wed 7/7.
- Acme (Tom / Procurement): flag any procurement constraints (PO timing, billing cadence).

Attached: ACME-2027-Renewal-Quote-v3.pdf (draft) and a draft SOW outline.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the formal quote and a suggested pilot schedule.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the recap, looks good. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The 120M tokens/month number is accurate but ~65% production, 35% dev/test. For the pilot we can carve out traffic from a staging pool and run on copies of production samples.
- For procurement: our standard PO cycle is ~30 days after final quote; finance prefers annual invoices but can accept quarterly if needed.
- Latency: for the summarization workload we need p95 under 800ms for agent UX, ideally <500ms for re-rank. Is that realistic on a Dedicated pool?

Can you confirm expected cost delta for the Dedicated pilot vs current consumption? Also, attach any short SLA language for Dedicated pools so I can flag to infra.

Thanks,
Tom

Hi all — quick technical follow-up from the call and the proposed pilot: 

Latency notes / recommended config:
- For the summarization workload (sequence lengths avg ~1,600 tokens), target Dedicated pool with GPUs that support fp16 + 4-bit quant profiles; this should get p95 into the 350–700ms range with continuous batching (depends on concurrency).
- For re-ranking (shorter sequences), use an optimized embedding workflow with batched requests — expected latency <200ms p95.
- Cold starts: we recommend a small warm standby (1 replica) during business hours to avoid cold-start spikes.

Batching & cost tips:
- Use adaptive micro-batching with a 40–60ms batch window for summarization to balance latency and throughput.
- We’ll ship a prebuilt config (batching settings + quant profile) as part of the pilot SOW.

I’ll attach a short KB link with example configs and runbook after this note. Happy to run a short 30-min tech deep-dive with your infra team during week of 7/12.

— Vivek
